_comment: R20 — the MCP twin of R19. M8 was fixed in `_gate_write`, which handle_bash and handle_argv call and handle_mcp does not, so `sf data delete record --sobject Account --record-id …` was refused through Bash and allowed through MCP. An agent meeting a refusal does not need to defeat it; it needs only to phrase the same request through the other surface. `no_divergent_twins` cannot see this — it compares same-named functions across modules and exempts per-gate entry points, which is exactly what these are — so `surfaces_agree` was added to compare verdicts rather than source. These fixtures pin the MCP surface specifically; the parity check pins the relationship between surfaces.

fixtures.id: R20 deny: MCP delete of a protected sObject by record Id
R20 deny: MCP delete, lowercase object name reaches the same table
R20 deny: MCP delete under the objectName spelling
R20 allow: MCP delete of a non-protected sObject by record Id
R20 allow: MCP update of a protected sObject by record Id stays ungated, as on argv
R20 allow: MCP read of a protected sObject
R20 deny: MCP where-delete of a protected sObject still refuses for its OWN reason
R20 deny: MCP bulk delete is unchanged by any of this
